topic_tag: a clause in a river-water treaty
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Writing in 1980, one legal historian called the seventh clause the treaty's ______.

worlds.passage: In 1922 two neighboring states signed a treaty dividing the water of a river that crossed both. Its seventh clause let the upstream state take more than its share in an emergency and left the upstream state's own governor to declare when one existed. Its governors declared emergencies in thirty-one of the next forty summers, asking nothing else of their neighbor, and in each such year the downstream state received about half the share the treaty promised it for the whole year. Writing in 1980, one legal historian called the seventh clause the treaty's ______.
worlds.explanation: The clause let one party decide for itself when it could exceed its share, and that party used it to take water the treaty otherwise promised the other, so the clause was the treaty's "loophole." "Lever" fails because the upstream state used the clause to take water directly and sought nothing else with it; "keystone" fails because the clause is an exception to the other terms, not the piece they rest on; "lottery" fails because the shortfalls followed the governors' declarations, not chance.

lever.quote: asking nothing else of their neighbor
lever.why: the clause was used to take water outright, not as pressure to win other concessions

keystone.quote: take more than its share in an emergency
keystone.why: the clause is an exception to the other terms, not the piece they all rest on

lottery.quote: the upstream state's own governor to declare
lottery.why: the outcome was decided by one party's choice, not by chance

worlds.passage: In 1922 two neighboring states signed a treaty dividing the water of a river that crossed both. Its seventh clause set the method for measuring the river's yearly flow, and every other clause stated each state's share as a fraction of the flow so measured. In 1961 a court struck the method down because the gauge it named had been removed decades earlier. The two states then spent nine years negotiating a new treaty from the beginning. Writing in 1980, one legal historian called the seventh clause the treaty's ______.
worlds.explanation: Every other clause was written in terms the seventh defined, so when it was struck down the states had to rebuild the whole treaty: it was the treaty's "keystone." "Loophole" fails because the clause let no party escape its obligations, and the court removed it for an outdated gauge, not for abuse; "lever" fails because no state used it to pressure the other; "lottery" fails because it was a fixed method of measurement, not a matter of chance.

loophole.quote: every other clause stated each state's share
loophole.why: the clause underlies the obligations rather than offering a way around them

lever.quote: negotiating a new treaty from the beginning
lever.why: the clause matters because the treaty collapsed without it, not because a state wielded it

lottery.quote: because the gauge it named had been removed
lottery.why: the clause failed for a concrete reason, not through any element of chance

worlds.passage: In 1922 two neighboring states signed a treaty dividing the water of a river that crossed both. Its seventh clause required the downstream state's consent before the upstream state could build any new dam on the river. Over forty years the upstream state proposed six dams, and each time the downstream state gave its consent only after winning something unrelated to water: a highway link, a share of a power plant, fishing rights. All six dams were built. Writing in 1980, one legal historian called the seventh clause the treaty's ______.
worlds.explanation: The downstream state used its power to withhold consent to win unrelated concessions, so the clause served as the treaty's "lever." "Loophole" fails because no one used the clause to escape an obligation: the downstream state granted consent every time and every dam was built; "keystone" fails because nothing says the other clauses depended on it; "lottery" fails because each outcome came from deliberate bargaining, not chance.

loophole.why: the clause was never used to evade anything; it was used as bargaining power and consent always followed

keystone.why: the clause matters as a tool one side used, not as the piece the treaty rests on

lottery.why: the results were won by bargaining, not left to chance

worlds.passage: In 1922 two neighboring states signed a treaty dividing the water of a river that crossed both. Its seventh clause fixed each year's shares by the depth of snow at a single mountain stake on one fixed day each spring. A late storm or an early thaw in the days around that date could double or halve a state's share for the whole year, and farmers in both states learned not to plant until that day's reading was announced. Writing in 1980, one legal historian called the seventh clause the treaty's ______.
worlds.explanation: Each year's shares turned on the weather at one stake on one day, so the clause made the division a matter of chance: the treaty's "lottery." "Loophole" fails because no party used the clause to escape its obligations; "lever" fails because neither state could steer the reading to press the other; "keystone" fails because nothing says the other clauses depended on it.

loophole.quote: farmers in both states learned not to plant
loophole.why: both states were equally at the mercy of the reading; neither exploited it

lever.quote: a late storm or an early thaw
lever.why: the outcome came from the weather, not from either state's pressure

keystone.quote: depth of snow at a single mountain stake
keystone.why: what makes the clause notable is its dependence on one chance reading, not that the treaty rests on it
